To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Z → μμ decay is the only LFV Z decay that can be measured at the TESLA Giga‐Z option; (ii) Z → eμ and Z → μe can be excluded with a 95% CL if the Giga‐ Z option of TESLA is realized; (iii) the Z → τe and Z → τμ decays are not accessible to the TESLA experiment.
the Z → μμ, Z → μe and Z → τe decays are all at the reach of TESLA.
the Giga‐ Z mode at TESLA is able to measure Z → μe at the 10-5 level and Z → τl at the 10 -4 level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the LFV decays Z → μe and Z → τl in the framework of Effective Lagrangians, and the comparison of the results with the SM predictions.
the following topics: - The effective lagrangian formalism and its application to the study of LFV Z decays. - The study of the Z → μl decay in the decoupling limit.
the phenomenological study of the Z → μl decay in the framework of the Standard Model (including radiative corrections) and its extensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Giga‐ Z mode in TESL A is the most appropriate way of measuring LFV Z decays.
the Giga‐ Z mode is the only way to probe Z → τl at the TESLA energy.
the TESLA experiment will be able to put strong restrictions on Lepton Flavour Physics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TESLA experiment is a good place for the study of LFV decays.
the TESLA experiment will be able to put strong bounds on the Z → lilj decay, and that it will provide the best measurement of the Z → eμ decay in the next 10‐15 years.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Z → μτ and Z → μe decays are very sensitive to new physics effects and that the TESLA Giga‐Z could provide a very good opportunity to test the LFV predictions.
